title: You Turned On Yardi Auto Reconciliation. Half Your Banks Did Not Work. Here Is What to Check First.
summary: Yardi auto reconciliation is not a feature toggle but a readiness project across six dimensions, and most portfolios stall because bank file compatibility, delivery reliability, and transaction code mapping are not addressed before activation.
body_markdown:
Yardi auto reconciliation setup sounds like a configuration step. In practice, it is a readiness project that spans bank connectivity, data formatting, account configuration, and GL alignment. Controllers activate the feature and discover that half their banks produce files Yardi cannot consume, transaction codes are unmapped, and GL posting cadence does not match bank data delivery. We often see 40% to 60% of banks in a real estate portfolio fail the first import test. The feature works. The data feeding it does not. This checklist identifies where most portfolios break and what to address before turning anything on.


## **File Format Compatibility**


Yardi expects bank data in BAI2 format. The first question is whether every bank produces a BAI2 file Yardi accepts without preprocessing. Request a sample file from every bank and attempt a test import. BAI2 file requirements are technically standardized but practically inconsistent. Some banks produce files with nonstandard field separators or missing trailer records. Others do not offer BAI2 at all and deliver only CSV or PDF. Every non BAI2 bank needs a defined conversion path or it stays outside auto reconciliation permanently.


## **Transaction Code Mapping**


Yardi uses transaction type codes to categorize bank transactions and match them against ledger entries. Each bank uses different codes for the same transaction types. A wire coded as type 195 at one bank must map to the same Yardi category as type 45 at another. We often see 10 to 20 unmapped or incorrectly mapped codes across a portfolio on first review. Each one is a matching failure waiting to happen.


## **Account Structure and GL Readiness**


Every bank account must map to the correct entity, property, and GL cash account in Yardi. Stale mappings from restructurings cause matches to post to the wrong property. We often see 5% to 10% of accounts carry outdated assignments. Equally important is GL posting cadence. Auto reconciliation matches bank transactions against GL entries. When AP and AR post weekly but bank data arrives daily, one side of the match is missing when the job runs. Matching rates drop 15% to 25% at properties with this cadence mismatch.


## **Data Delivery Reliability**


If bank data does not arrive before the reconciliation job runs, those accounts are skipped.


- Banks with consistent SFTP delivery and predictable timing are ready for automated ingestion


- Banks requiring manual portal downloads are not ready unless a retrieval mechanism is added


- Banks with inconsistent delivery windows need monitoring to confirm arrival before each cycle


- Banks that deliver only on request or only as PDF require a format conversion path before anything else


The Yardi bank rec checklist starts and ends with whether every file arrives automatically, on time, every day.


## **Exception Workflow**


Auto reconciliation will produce unmatched items. Without a defined workflow for who reviews them, how frequently, and what the escalation path is, exceptions accumulate into a backlog that undermines the value of automation. Property accounting automation requires exception governance from day one, not after the backlog has grown.


## **Key Takeaways**


Yardi auto reconciliation setup spans six dimensions and most portfolios are not ready across all of them. The gaps concentrate at the bank data layer where format inconsistency, delivery unreliability, and code misalignment prevent the feature from running completely. Platforms like Arpari close these gaps by normalizing bank files, managing delivery, and maintaining transaction code mappings centrally. The hardest items on the checklist are handled by the platform before the controller touches them. The reconciliation engine is ready. The question is whether the data feeding it is ready too.
